summary.headline: Domestic revenue fell 1.9% YoY to INR111 crore in Q1 FY27, while EBITDA rose 42% to INR8.8 crore on cost cuts and Digital grew 43.3%.
summary.overview: Management attributed the soft quarter to the West Asia conflict, which caused event cancellations, curtailed artist travel and lower advertiser demand across media. Digital (Gaana) revenue rose 43.3% YoY to INR31.1 crore and its losses narrowed, with management targeting breakeven as soon as possible. Cost rationalisation drove the EBITDA and PAT improvement, with non-digital EBITDA up 7.4% and PAT up 85%. Management gave no numerical guidance and said the Events business is H2-weighted.

financial_highlights.change: +43.3% YoY; 30.2% of total revenue vs 23% last year
vs INR17.9 crore last year (~19% growth)
vs INR9.8 crore last year (~15% lower)

segments.name: Radio (FCT advertising)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR62.2 crore, about 56% of total revenue. Inventory utilisation fell about 8% while rates rose about 4%. Volume market share was about 27-28%.

segments.name: Digital (Gaana)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR31.1 crore (+43.3%), with Gaana at INR21.4 crore (+19%). Losses fell to INR8.3 crore from INR9.8 crore. Around 70% of subscribers are on profitable price points.

segments.name: Non-FCT / Events
segments.commentary: Non-FCT revenue INR17.5 crore, hit by event cancellations and artist travel disruption. Management says Events is about 35:65 H1:H2 and that Q1 and Q2 are seasonally subdued.

guidance_outlook: Management gave no formal profitability guidance for FY27.
Traditional media (Radio, TV, Print) expected to stay subdued through FY27.
Events expected to grow and to be strong from Q2 onward; some international artist concerts moved from Q1 into Q2.
Cost-model restructuring (station networking, AI, new broadcast tools) expected to benefit all quarters of FY27, with no quantum given.
Gaana targeted for breakeven as soon as possible; a quarter-level slip is possible if customer acquisition costs rise.
Gaana monthly pricing is about 10% below competition; annual pricing retains headroom; price raised to INR799.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning figures were discussed on the call.
demand_pricing: Radio advertiser demand remained soft in Q1 FY27 owing to macro and geopolitical uncertainty; management said the pressure extends across TV, print and outdoor.
Radio rates improved about 4% despite inventory utilisation falling about 8%.
Gaana subscription pricing moved to INR799; the company says it is the only pure-subscription service in India, versus free and premium tiers at competitors.
Management says the industry is moving toward subscription, citing Universal Music's 72-hour exclusivity for premium subscribers and Spotify's free-tier restrictions.

qa_highlights.question: Is the radio advertising weakness only due to West Asia, and will the company diversify beyond media?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the weakness is an industry-wide shift away from traditional advertising plus geopolitical impact. It said the three verticals are Radio, Digital and Events, and that the company will stay in media while experimenting with AI.

qa_highlights.question: Will Events cancellations be recovered, and what is the seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Some events moved into Q2, including international artist concerts. Events is roughly 35:65 H1:H2 and Q1 and Q2 are normally subdued.

qa_highlights.question: What cost savings can be expected and what is the profitability outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify savings and cited networking of stations, AI and new broadcast tools. It declined to give profitability guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What are Gaana's subscriber profitability and path to breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of subscribers are at profitable margins. Management aims for breakeven as soon as possible, with the lower-value subscriber base being churned out.

qa_highlights.question: Would a buyback be considered with INR390 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a Board discussion and that the feedback would be taken.

qa_highlights.question: Has industry subscriber growth moderated, and how is pricing positioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said annual pricing has headroom, monthly pricing is about 10% below competition, and the industry is moving toward subscription. It did not give subscriber growth data.

risks_watch: Radio advertising remains soft; management expects traditional media to stay subdued through FY27.
Gaana still loss-making at INR8.3 crore in the quarter; breakeven timing is open, and CAC increases could delay it.
Event cancellations and artist travel disruption from the West Asia conflict, with Q2 recovery dependent on the timing of international concerts.
Buyback request from shareholders is pending a Board decision; no commitment made.
Cost-saving quantum not disclosed, so the EBITDA trajectory beyond Q1 is unclear.
summary.management_tone: Confident about Digital and Events and about the subscription model, but cautious and non-committal on Radio demand, cost savings and profitability. Management declined to quantify savings, guide on profitability or commit to a buyback.
key_quotes: Encouraging to note that despite prevailing macro headwinds, the non -digital business improved profitability, delivering EBITDA growth of 7.4% and PAT growth of 85% during the quarter.
